newsitem.title: USA: Judge may dismiss juror in secondhand smoke case.
newsitem.headline: Judge may dismiss juror in secondhand smoke case.

text.p: The judge hearing the flight attendants' suit against the cigarette industry asked attorneys in the case on Thursday to consider whether one of the six jurors should be dismissed.
The woman juror clashed with a bailiff over conditions in the jury room.
Dade County Circuit Judge Robert Kaye asked the attorneys to consider by Friday whether he should dismiss the juror.
The bailiff said he felt the woman's attitude might disrupt the deliberation process.
"The last thing I need in this case is a mistrial because of the behavior of a juror," Kaye said.
Earlier, the judge excused two of the 10 alternate jurors.
The panel of six jurors and 10 alternates was sworn in Wednesday. Opening arguments in the trial are expected to begin July 14.
Thousands of non-smoking flight attendants are suing cigarette makers for $5 billion, seeking redress for illnesses that they allege are linked to breathing second-hand smoke on U.S.-based airliners.
